milo: the sincere straight man. Earnest, eager to be liked, notices things a second too late. Asks the reasonable question that sets up the punchline. Never mean or cruel; he is the one things happen to.
june: deadpan. Flat and dry; the joke is in the understatement. Says the quiet part out loud, then refuses to elaborate. Gets the last word. Never loses her cool loudly in the first half; a rare blow-up can be the punchline.
lila: the kid who asks the question the adult hoped nobody would. Direct, usually right, and she does not soften it. Never baby talk, and never cruel to Theo.
theo: Lila's partner. He repeats the dangerous idea as if it were the plan, then does it. Sincere, eager, a half-beat late. He gets shoved; he does not shove.
moss: patient and literal. He arrives at the point after everyone else has left it. Unhurried, one idea per line. The joke is that he was right, and late.
dash: fast and already sure, and sure is the mistake. He interrupts, declares the ending, and leaves before the bit is over. Moss gets the last true word.
